Method of Attack: Malvertizing campaigns using fake pages mimicking the official WinSCP website to push malware-ridden installers
Victims search for 'WinSCP Download' on Bing or Google, click malicious ads leading to fake WinSCP clone sites
Victim downloads ISO containing setup.exe and msi.dll; setup.exe executes msi.dll which extracts a Python folder and installs trojanized python310.dll
Persistence established via registry run key 'Python' pointing to pythonw.exe
pythonw.exe loads modified obfuscated python310.dll containing Cobalt Strike beacon connecting to command-and-control server

Subsequent use of tools like AdFind, PowerShell scripts, AccessChk64, Findstr, PowerView, Python scripts, PsExec, BitsAdmin, Curl, AnyDesk, KillAV BAT script, PuTTY SCP client, and SpyBoy 'Terminator' EDR/AV disabler
Impacted Systems: Windows systems used by system administrators, web admins, IT professionals
Attack Vector: Malvertising via Google and Bing search ads leading to fake WinSCP download sites
Indicators of Compromise: Fake domain names similar to winscp.net such as winsccp.com
ISO file containing setup.exe and msi.dll
Registry run key named 'Python' with value 'C:\Users\Public\Music\python\pythonw.exe'
Presence of trojanized python310.dll and pythonw.exe
Cobalt Strike beacon connecting to command-and-control servers
Use of tools like AdFind, PowerShell commands, AccessChk64, Findstr, PowerView, LaZagne password recovery tool, PsExec, BitsAdmin, Curl, AnyDesk, KillAV BAT script, PuTTY SCP client
